newsitem.title: UK: Dlr steady in Europe as Buba holds rates, stg soft.
newsitem.headline: Dlr steady in Europe as Buba holds rates, stg soft.

text.p: The dollar remained mostly steady at the European midsession, orbiting the 1.56 mark level after the Bundesbank's decision to keeps rates on hold and fresh falls in sterling against the mark and dollar.
Sterling dropped over 3.5 cents against the dollar and over four pfennigs against the mark in morning Europe before posting a slight recovery by the midsession.

Dealers attributed the pound's fresh falls to a continuation of profit-taking from its recent highs combined with benign comments from Bank of England Governor Eddie George on further UK interest rate hikes.

"This is more adjustment of positions, it's not explicitly from George's comments," said Tim Fox, economist at Standard Chartered Bank in London. "The market is accepting that the stronger UK growth, higher rate argument has been overdone."

The UK central bank's George said he saw no need for a dramatic rise in rates but expected one before the next general election which must be held by May 1997. Analysts said these were the most benign rate comments from George for several months.
Cable was trading at $1.6210/20 at 1221 GMT after touching a session low of $1.6103. It stood at $1.6410/20 late Wednesday.
Sterling/mark was also easier, trading at 2.5310/20 after touching a low of 2.5165 marks. It was at 2.5620/31 Wednesday.
The Bundesbank's decision to leave rates steady caused few surprises.
Wednesday's firm third quarter German GDP cooled earlier speculation of a near-term rate cut but analysts said inflation still posed little threat following today's rise in German unemployment.
The pan-German November adjusted jobless rate rose a higher than expected seasonally adjusted 50,000, pushing the adjusted unemployment rate to 10.7 percent from 10.6 percent in October.
Dollar/mark was trading at 1.5597/07 at 1241 GMT compared with 1.5625/30 late Wednesday.
Dollar/yen remained steady above the 112.50 level with trade cautious ahead of a Japanese television interview with Ministry of Finance official Eisuke Sakakibara at 1400 GMT.
The yen had firmed overnight amid comments from a former Ministry of Finance official that the Bank of Japan was keen to change the official discount rate as soon as possible.
By 1253 GMT, the dollar against the yen stood at 112.71/76 from 113.07/12 Wednesday.
